journey.name: a single lightning payment above 10% of a new channel is received
journey.description:
Bitkit's node cannot announce channels, so it only accepts unannounced ones. Until LDK Node 0.7.0-rc.77 it let the channel partner put at most 10% of the channel value in flight, so a single incoming payment above 10% of the channel failed with no route, even when the channel had the receiving capacity. From rc.77 a channel opened by an updated app accepts up to its full value. Channels opened before the update keep the 10% limit.
Precondition: an onboarded regtest wallet with a new channel from the LSP that has receiving capacity, opened on LDK Node 0.7.0-rc.77 or later, connected to the LSP (README.md, Backend preconditions). This build cannot buy a channel from Blocktank (synonymdev/bitkit-ios#1097), so open it on a build from before that change with an rc.77 node, with Transfer To Spending, and install this build over it (README.md, Getting a Lightning channel). The LSP node pays the invoices with the lsp helper (borrowed from the sibling Android checkout, see README.md).

actions.action: Open Settings, then the "Advanced" tab, then "Lightning Connections", open the new connection and note its total size and receiving capacity
Go back to Receive and create a Lightning invoice for an amount between 15% and 90% of the connection's total size that is also below its receiving capacity (for example 30% of the size)
Pay it from the LSP node with the same helper call
Verify the payment arrives: the received sheet shows the amount, and the spending balance grows by it
Regression check: with a build on LDK Node 0.7.0-rc.76 the same second payment fails with no route and Bitkit shows nothing
